rulings.rationale: The title remains recoverable as a formal threshold while requiring the dialogue it governs for interpretation.
rulings.counterevidence: The heading governs the whole book and is too thin for context-free interpretation.
rulings.rejected_alternative: Merge 1:1 into the 1:2-4 complaint and blur the heading-to-lament transition.

rulings.rationale: Cry, witnessed disorder, and judicial result form one causal complaint before the imperative answer opens at 1:5.
rulings.counterevidence: Verse 1:4 has aphoristic wording and strong isolated-retrieval pressure.
rulings.rejected_alternative: Split 1:4 as an independent law-and-justice maxim or surface 1:2-3 apart from its result.

rulings.rationale: Announcement, named agent, military characteristics, violence, conquest, and final culpability resolve as one divine-answer movement.
rulings.counterevidence: Verse 1:6 is a strong naming turn and 1:11 shifts from description to evaluation.
rulings.rejected_alternative: Detach 1:5, split 1:5-6 from 1:7-11, or surface catalogue fragments.

rulings.rationale: The difficult premise in 1:12 and the concrete net imagery jointly build the second complaint, which closes before the watchpost posture.
rulings.counterevidence: The 1:12 wording is textually difficult and fish imagery turns sharply at 1:14.
rulings.rejected_alternative: Split 1:12-13 from 1:14-17, isolate 1:12, or extend the complaint through 2:1.

rulings.rationale: This liminal verse closes complaint posture and opens expectation without becoming part of the divine speech.
rulings.counterevidence: The one-verse hinge is dependent on both neighboring movements and cannot interpret itself.
rulings.rejected_alternative: Attach 2:1 backward to 1:12-2:1 or forward to 2:1-5 and suppress its bridge function.

rulings.rationale: Verse 2:5 supplies the oppressor antecedent and bridge for the nations taunt, completing the answer prologue without detaching 2:4.
rulings.counterevidence: Strong internal pressures occur at 2:3|4 and 2:4|5, and the syntax and renderings in 2:4-5 remain difficult.
rulings.rejected_alternative: Split 2:2-3, 2:4, and 2:5; include 2:1; or extend the unit through 2:6.

rulings.rationale: The introduction cannot be detached from the woe embedded in its own verse, and 2:7-8 supply that accusation its reversal.
rulings.counterevidence: The introduction formally governs all five woes rather than only the first.
rulings.rejected_alternative: Surface 2:6 as a heading alone, split accusation from reversal, or retain all 2:6-20 as one thin-pass block.

rulings.rationale: Household self-protection, self-condemnation, and answering building materials complete one accusation-consequence movement.
rulings.counterevidence: The building-material witness can anticipate the blood-built-city woe that opens at 2:12.
rulings.rejected_alternative: Split 2:11 from 2:9-10 or isolate the memorable wall witness.

rulings.rationale: Violent construction, labor for fire, and contrasting worldwide knowledge form the accusation and its completed reversal.
rulings.counterevidence: Verse 2:14 has broad proverbial and canonical resonance and attracts independent retrieval.
rulings.rejected_alternative: Detach 2:14 as a positive oracle or split 2:12 from 2:13-14.

rulings.rationale: Manipulated intoxication, reciprocal shame, divine cup, and returning violence form a complete mirrored judgment.
rulings.counterevidence: Verse 2:17 broadens beyond the drinking image and echoes the violence formula of 2:8.
rulings.rejected_alternative: Split 2:15-16 from 2:17 or detach the violence catalogue.

rulings.rationale: Maker trusts mute product, wood and stone lack breath, and living presence commands silence; the semantic reversal outweighs the internal marker under the larger-unit tie rule.
rulings.counterevidence: The samekh after 2:18 and new woe at 2:19 make the Hebrew split a substantial child-route dissent.

rulings.rationale: Title and opening petition are formally distinct but safer as one recoverable prayer opening than as isolated metadata.
rulings.counterevidence: The nominal superscription and direct petition are verse-complete forms with a real 3:1|2 seam.
rulings.rejected_alternative: Surface 3:1 and 3:2 separately or merge the petition into 3:3-7.

rulings.rationale: Arrival and cosmic-national trembling form a coherent advent stanza inside the larger theophany.
rulings.counterevidence: Selah inside 3:3 and the first-person I-saw turn at 3:7 create internal stanza pressure.
rulings.rejected_alternative: Split at Selah inside 3:3, isolate 3:7, or retain all 3:3-15 as one surface block.

rulings.rationale: The horses and sea at 3:8 and 3:15 form an inclusio, while actor, verbal chain, weapons, and combat continue across the strongest internal marker seam.
rulings.counterevidence: Selah, WLC-family pe, WEB line break, and the first-person object at 3:14 make 3:13|14 the strongest child-seam dissent in Habakkuk.
rulings.rejected_alternative: Surface 3:8-13 and 3:14-15 as siblings, or isolate the salvation-purpose clause.

rulings.rationale: Fear and waiting supply the situation, crop and herd failure the concession, and rejoicing plus strength the complete response and prayer close.
rulings.counterevidence: The first-person return, concessive marker, emphatic response, and subscription are real internal turns.
rulings.rejected_alternative: Split 3:16 from 3:17-19, surface 3:17-18 alone, or detach the 3:19 confession or subscription.
